title: Inflation, scarcity, and rural vulnerability deepen
detail: Postwar economic weakness, distribution failures, black-market pressures, and rising prices had already pushed many households toward crisis before the monsoon floods intensified the emergency.

title: Special Powers Act is enacted
detail: The Special Powers Act expanded preventive detention and extraordinary state authority, indicating that the government was responding to instability with a more coercive legal framework.

title: Floods and food-distribution failures worsen famine conditions
detail: Severe flooding and a weak food-rationing system accelerated entitlement collapse in rural areas, where laborers and small peasants were hit hardest.

title: Starvation, displacement, and distress migration spread
detail: As the crisis deepened, people sold assets, left villages, and moved toward towns in search of food, while mortality rose sharply and public confidence in the state deteriorated.

title: Crisis politics narrows the path toward 1975
detail: The famine and the turn toward exceptional state power hardened the atmosphere of fear, blame, and centralized control that preceded the BAKSAL transition and the violence of 1975.
